Understanding disability, caregiving, and health across the life course.

Social work · University of Toronto

Liangqi (Cecilia)
Shen

PhD student

I am a PhD student at the Factor-Inwentash Faculty of Social Work, University of Toronto, supervised by Dr. Esme Fuller-Thomson. My research examines how disabilities shape the lives of individuals, their caregivers, and their families. I enjoy reading, writing, and theoretical thinking.

I am originally from Anshun, Guizhou, where I grew up before leaving for university. Beyond my hometown and Toronto, I have also lived in Tianjin, Hangzhou, Ann Arbor, and Chicago. Outside of academia, I love spending time with my family and enjoying local life together.

Published work.

I bring a life-course perspective to the connections between disability, family care, and later-life well-being.

Intellectual & developmental disabilitiesFamily caregivingAging & health

My work draws on large longitudinal and national datasets, including CCHS, HRS, MIDUS, and NSCH, alongside primary data collection and systematic reviews across Canada, the United States, and China. My practice experience includes supporting children with autism and their families in Hangzhou, China.

Places I’ve called home.

Here are a few of my recommendations for places to explore and things to do in the cities I’ve lived in.

Toronto
The Distillery Winter Village and St. Lawrence Market. You can also enjoy authentic food from around the world!
Ann Arbor
Football games, kayaking, Washtenaw Dairy (personal favorite: toasted coconut ice cream), and Pinckney Recreation Area.
Chicago
An architecture tour, the Jane Addams Hull-House (especially for social workers), Lincoln Park Zoo, and the beaches.
Anshun
Local snacks, rice noodles (my comfort food), waterfalls, and caves.
Tianjin
The Five Great Avenues and Jianbing Guozi (street food).
Hangzhou
West Lake, especially the Nine Creeks area. Visit Longwu for a green tea experience.
